newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway bourse hits life high in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Norway bourse hits life high in light trade.

text.p: The Norwegian stock exchange hit a record closing high on Friday in the wake of overnight gains on Wall Street, but trade was thin at 466 million crowns.
The Oslo Total Index finished 1.8 percent higher at 960.26 points.

The bullish trade was led by blue chips with Norsk Hydro gaining 2.72 percent to close at 340 crowns, Kvaerner B shares rising 4.15 percent to 276 crowns and Orkla B shares going up 1.79 percent to 398 crowns.
Norsk Hydro, which has a 20 percent weighting on the Total index, was the most traded share at 59 million crowns.

Apart from being boosted by Wall Street, the Oslo Bourse was driven up by increased liquidity for mutual funds. Small-time savers are paying into such funds in late December to carry tax breaks into January for the so-called "January effect".
"A lot of small-time savers have been active today," one dealer said.
"I think we are seeing the January effect," another said.
